alerts.title: Creatinine not monitored for 15 months on TDF+DTG
alerts.message: TDF can cause renal toxicity and DTG affects renal tubular secretion, making periodic creatinine monitoring essential. The patient's only creatinine result (88 umol/L) was obtained 478 days before this visit — over 15 months ago. No renal function test was ordered today despite the patient being on a TDF-containing regimen for approximately 3 years. The latest creatinine value is within normal range, but without a recent or trending result, current renal safety of TDF cannot be confirmed. The clinician's plan of 'routine follow-up, no issues' does not include any renal monitoring.

evidence.recommended_action: Order serum creatinine and urinalysis to assess current renal function given TDF use. Establish regular renal monitoring schedule per guideline recommendations.

alerts.title: Viral load 40 copies/mL near detection threshold
alerts.message: The patient's viral load was 40 copies/mL on 2025-10-01, 113 days before this visit. While this is below common suppression thresholds, it sits near the lower limit of quantification for many assays. A single low-level value may represent a blip, but without a prior viral load for comparison, a trend cannot be established. No repeat viral load was ordered at this visit. Low-level viremia can occasionally precede treatment failure, particularly if adherence is declining. The patient reports good adherence and feels well, which supports continued suppression but does not substitute for confirmatory testing.

evidence.recommended_action: Consider repeating viral load at next scheduled visit to confirm sustained suppression and establish a trend, particularly given the low-level result.

alerts.title: ADR screening not documented at this encounter
alerts.message: Guidelines state that for each encounter, all health workers should screen for suspected adverse drug reactions using the Drug Safety Screening checklist. The clinician documented 'no issues' and 'routine follow-up' but did not record completion of a structured ADR screening. The patient is on DTG, which is associated with neuropsychiatric symptoms including insomnia, headaches, anxiety, and mood changes per the guideline checklist. The patient reported no new complaints, which provides some reassurance, but guideline-directed screening should be explicitly documented.

evidence.recommended_action: Complete and document the Drug Safety Screening checklist at this encounter, including specific screening for DTG-related neuropsychiatric symptoms.
